actualScienceFindings: Bottom arenium attacked carbon incorrectly bears bonded E+ and a second E instead of neutral E and H.
Bottom ring has two full positive charges and an aromatic-style six-edge dashed interior, not a valid singly charged nonaromatic sigma-complex contributor.
Product retains one E but the precursor has two Es and no explicit H at attacked carbon; removal labeled H+ therefore fails atom/substituent conservation.
Upper intermediate also attaches charged E+ while carrying a ring plus; a valid singly charged intermediate needs neutral attached E.
existingGoodStyleKept: White background and bold legible black molecular outlines
Wide composition and large molecular motifs
correctionScope: One corrected raster candidate only, no active integration, original texts KEEP. Simplified three-stage substitution focuses on exact E/H and charge conservation, temporary aromaticity loss/restoration.
